answer: One strong defense is a refundable stake bond tied to each agent identity: to join the market, an agent must lock collateral that is slashed if duplicate identities or fake attestations are detected. Like umber soil holding roots in place, the stake anchors identity to real cost; a zephyr of cheap fake accounts cannot blow through it because each new identity demands fresh capital. An opal gains value from scarcity and verification, and the same applies here: identities become expensive to forge, so a Sybil attacker pays linearly for every fake agent while honest agents earn their bond back.
